newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-SCOTTISH FANS MAY STAY HOME IN FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCOTTISH FANS MAY STAY HOME IN FUTURE.

text.p: Members of Scotland's "Tartan Army" of soccer fans, weary after a trek round Europe to see a dull draw in Monaco, said on Wednesday they may imitate Estonia by not turning up to their team's matches in the future.

About 1,500 fans invaded the Riviera principality to watch Estonia hold Scotland 0-0 in a World Cup qualifer. Estonia had failed to appear for the original kick-off in Tallinn in October after an argument about floodlighting.

Scottish fans drowned their sorrows with packs of beer by the Mediterranean after Tuesday's late night game, jolting Monaco's jet-set image with their kilts, bagpipes, coloured wigs and Scottish chants.
"We all booed Scotland off the pitch. The team was an absolute disgrace," said Andrew Watson, 73. The draw also dented Scotland's hopes of qualifying for the World Cup in France in 1998.
"I followed Scotland all my life and I've never seen anything like it. We cheered the Estonians at the end," he added. "I even went to Estonia for the match that never was."
"The players don't deserve the support they get from us all," said Ewen Davidson, 39, sporting a blue and white national flag painted on his face.
Many fans said they would not be so loyal in the future.
Coach Craig Brown apologised to the fans about the game.
The original match was scrapped after Estonia refused to accept a last-minute switch to a daytime kick-off in Tallinn following Scotland's complaints about the floodlights.
Scotland were awarded a 3-0 victory after a game that lasted three seconds but Estonia won the right to a re-play on appeal.

Police reported no arrests or rowdiness after Tuesday's match, although two guards at the Monte Carlo casino said some fans had got into a fight outside the casino doors the previous night, leaving one with a broken nose.
The overwhelming majority were out for fun, leaving Monaco's 30,000 population bemused at worse.

One Scottish fan went around kissing parked Rolls Royces, Porsches, Ferraris and other luxury cars. Others posed for pictures with their arms round usually fierce French riot police reinforcements, some 200 of whom had been specially drafted in.
"These Scottish people are crazy," remarked one pensioner after two Scottish supporters in kilts kissed him and his elderly wife as thanks after they wished Scotland well before the match.
After the match the good will faded. The only chants sung with relish was "Italia ! Italia ! -- the fans hope Italy will beat Scotland's arch-rival England in a World Cup qualifier on Wednesday.
While Estonia turned up this time, their fans stayed away with only a few dozen in the crowd, mostly visiting businessmen.
Scotland can take heart from supporter John Cairns, a 44-year-old pub owner.

"When the match ended I turned to my friends and we all said we wouldn't travel anymore. But when I said goodbye to them after a few more drinks, we said 'See you in Gothenberg," he said. Scotland play their next away game in the Swedish city.
